Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

I. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

II. Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is not in row echelon form since the leading entry ${a}_{43}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated). 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is not in row echelon form since the leading entry ${c}_{32}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated). 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $A$ and $C$ are **not** in row echelon form.
